articles.title: India accelerates geothermal power push to diversify renewables - The New Indian Express
articles.content: NEW DELHI: India is moving towards generating power from Earth’s internal heart and underground water reservoirs and stepped up efforts to tap its vast geothermal energy resources, seeking to establish the largely untapped source of renewable energy as a reliable component of its clean energy mix. With the potential to provide round-the-clock power, geothermal energy is emerging as a promising avenue for strengthening energy security, reducing dependence on conventional fuels and advancing the country's commitment to achieving Net Zero emissions by 2070. Given its considerable geothermal potential, India is now moving towards translating resource assessments into practical applications through policy initiatives, international partnerships and pilot projects. The National Policy on Geothermal Energy, notified in September 2025, provides a framework for systematic exploration, development and utilisation of these resources, with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) serving as the nodal ministry for its implementation. A senior official source said geothermal power offers India a dependable and indigenous means of diversifying its renewable energy portfolio as the country accelerated its clean energy transition. Geothermal power generation involves converting the Earth's natural heat into electricity by tapping underground reservoirs of hot water and steam. Deep wells bring these resources to the surface, where steam drives a turbine connected to a generator. "This process resembles conventional thermal power generation", the official said. According to official sources, the Geological Survey of India (GSI) has mapped 381 hot springs across the country, while identified 10 geothermal provinces. India's theoretical geothermal resource potential is estimated at nearly 10.6 GW, with 42 sites recognised as promising for electricity generation and direct heat applications. India’s 10 identified provinces are in the Himalayan Geothermal Province, Naga-Lusai, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Son Narmada Tapi (SONATA), West Coast, Cambay Graben, Aravalli, Mahanadi, Godavari and South Indian Cratonic regions. India's geothermal development received a significant boost in July 2026, when the ONGC Energy Centre commissioned the country's first two geothermal wells at Puga Valley in Ladakh. Situated at an altitude of over 14,000 feet, Puga is considered one of India's most promising geothermal locations because of its hot springs and underground heat reserves. The two wells, each 1,000 metres deep, will facilitate reservoir evaluation and pave the way for India's first 1-megawatt demonstration geothermal power project. Their commissioning marks an important step towards moving the country from resource assessment to actual power generation. Government sources said, "From notifying the National Policy on Geothermal Energy to commissioning the country's first two geothermal wells at Puga Valley, Ladakh, India has moved decisively from planning to implementation." Sources further added that growing pilot projects and international collaborations were expanding geothermal applications beyond electricity generation to heating, geo-tourism and agriculture. Geothermal energy originates from the heat stored beneath the Earth's surface. The planet's internal temperature increases with depth, with the mantle reaching approximately 3,700 degrees Celsius at its boundary with the core, while core temperatures range between 5,000 and 6,000 degrees Celsius. articles.title: Reversing the Exodus: How India's 'First Villages' Along the China Border Are Thriving Again
articles.content: SHARE Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced on Sunday that out-migration from 40 villages bordering China in Arunachal Pradesh has effectively halted, with local populations now on the rise. Speaking at a cooperative conference in the state amid ongoing local protests over a proposed dam project, Shah attributed this demographic shift to expanded employment opportunities, improved healthcare, reliable electricity, and piped water reaching remote hilltops. By emphasizing tangible grassroots development, the Centre sought to reassure residents of its long-term commitment to the frontier region. Contents Empowering Local Cooperatives and Security Ties A Blueprint for Self-Reliance and Prosperity Reframing India’s “First Villages” Strategic Security and Centre-State Coordination Empowering Local Cooperatives and Security Ties A central pillar of the government’s border strategy involves integrating rural economies directly with security forces stationed in the state. Shah revealed that the Home Ministry has strictly mandated that the Indian Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) procure fresh produce locally rather than sourcing supplies from distant cities like Tezpur or Guwahati. Currently, local women operating through agricultural cooperatives supply dairy products, eggs, vegetables, millets, and flour to troops. This direct procurement model not only injects steady income into rural households and revitalizes local farming, but also strengthens day-to-day camaraderie between border residents and security personnel. - Advertisement - If you enjoyed reading this article, you can help support our journalism by adding OHeraldo as a preferred source. A Blueprint for Self-Reliance and Prosperity Outlining a comprehensive vision for Arunachal Pradesh’s future, Shah urged cooperative institutions and women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to spearhead a movement toward self-reliance in essential food production. He identified four primary pillars for the state’s growth: employment, education, healthcare, and the economic prosperity of every household. To formalize this trajectory, the Home Minister unveiled the “Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047,” a multi-decade roadmap designed to modernize and expand the cooperative sector. Alongside this blueprint, he rolled out 199 development projects valued at Rs 110.95 crore across 11 border districts and dispatched Mobile Medical Units to bring healthcare directly to isolated communities. Reframing India’s “First Villages” During his address, Shah underscored the ideological shift spearheaded by Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding India’s frontiers. Historically, remote settlements along international boundaries were referred to as the “country’s last villages,” a label that often reflected decades of administrative neglect. Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, the central government has rebranded these settlements as the “country’s first villages,” asserting that frontier communities hold the foremost claim to national development and infrastructure. Strategic Security and Centre-State Coordination The outreach followed a high-level security and development review chaired by Shah in Itanagar on Saturday. Alongside Chief Minister Pema Khandu, the Deputy Chief Minister, and Union Minister Kiren Rijiju, Shah spent nearly four hours mapping out future infrastructure priorities and assessing law and order along Arunachal Pradesh’s sensitive 1,126-kilometer border with China. Assuring the state leadership of full central backing without bureaucratic delays, Shah’s visit combined strategic border management with targeted economic outreach to stabilize and develop India’s northeastern frontier. articles.title: Bengaluru's SpaceFields successfully tests and hot-fires Rocket -Assisted Take-Off (RATO ...
articles.content: Home Trending News Startup News Bengaluru's SpaceFields successfully tests and hot-fires Rocket-Assisted Take-Off (RATO) Boosters at IISc facility Bengaluru's SpaceFields successfully tests and hot-fires Rocket-Assisted Take-Off (RATO) Boosters at IISc facility Bengaluru-based aerospace startup SpaceFields successfully tests and hot-fires various Rocket-Assisted Take-Off (RATO) Boosters at the IISc facility. By Ishita Ganguly 22 Nov 2026 00:06 IST Follow Us New Update SpaceFields successfully tests and hot-fires Rocket-Assisted Take-Off (RATO) Boosters SpaceFields has successfully tested and hot-fired various Rocket-Assisted Take-Off (RATO) boosters at its propulsion testing facility at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru. RATO boosters are auxiliary rocket propulsion units designed to provide additional thrust during the initial take-off of an aircraft or unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). They can be particularly useful when an aircraft needs additional assistance to take off from a short runway, operate with a heavier payload or function in challenging conditions. Such testing helps engineers assess the performance and reliability of propulsion hardware under controlled conditions. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source Also read: General Autonomy wins gold in India's first RobotDog race as quadruped PARAM clocks 4.3 m/s top speed Startup founded by 3 engineering graduates The Bengaluru-based startup, incubated at the Indian Institute of Science, was founded in 2021 by Apurwa Masook, Sudarshan Samal and Rounak Agrawal. The founders' journey began during their college days at Veer Surendra Sai University of Technology (VSSUT), Burla, Odisha. The three came together through the university's student rocketry initiative, VSSUT Satellite Launch Vehicle (VSLV), which became India's first student rocketry team. The team went on to design and successfully launch seven sounding rocket missions. Their experience in building rockets, developing propulsion systems and conducting experiments gave them the confidence to establish a commercial aerospace venture. Their ambition was to develop advanced propulsion technologies in India and make them available for both space and defence applications. Building next-generation propulsion systems SpaceFields focuses on designing and manufacturing solid-propellant rocket motors and customised propulsion systems. The company's product development includes solid rocket boosters, UAV RATO motors, pyrotechnic systems and other specialised propulsion solutions. It is also working on technologies for rockets, drones and emerging aerospace platforms. One of its major achievements came in 2023, when it unveiled and tested an aerospike rocket engine. In September 2024, the company successfully conducted a hot-fire test of its aerospike rocket engine at its IISc Challakere facility. It reported a peak thrust of 2,000 newtons during the test. Another successful hot-firing campaign was reported in January 2025, demonstrating a peak thrust of 13.42 kN. Support from IISc and the Indian startup ecosystem The Indian Institute of Science has played an important role in SpaceFields' journey. SpaceFields has also received support through government-backed startup programmes, including the Startup India Seed Fund and grants from the governments of Karnataka and Odisha, as well as Boeing India. In February 2024, the company raised $800,000 (approximately ₹6.5 crore) in its first institutional funding round. articles.title: India's First Bullet Train Project Hits Electrification Milestone As 50-Km Surat–Bilimora ...
articles.content: Nov 22, 2026 | Updated 08:59 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . The Mumbai–Ahmedabad Bullet Train project achieved a major electrification milestone with the successful energisation of the Overhead Equipment (OHE) system along the approximately 50-km Surat–Bilimora section in Gujarat on Friday (20 November). The development marks a key step towards further testing of India's first high-speed rail corridor, with the electrical system covering both Up and Down lines on the elevated alignment. In a statement, the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL), which is the implementing agency for the mega project, said that energisation will be carried out progressively in smaller sections, under the close supervision of the technical teams to ensure safety and compliance with prescribed procedures. The Mumbai–Ahmedabad Bullet Train corridor is equipped with an advanced 2x25 kV Overhead Traction System, one of the sophisticated electrification technologies used for high-speed rail systems worldwide. The electrification network comprises 14 strategically located Traction Substations (TSS) along the 508 km corridor. These substations will receive power from the National grid and supply it to the overhead traction system used by high-speed trains. The first Traction Substation at Bilimora in Gujarat's Navsari district has completed installation works in the control panel, changeover switch, transformer and circuit breaker buildings. The TSS in Gujarat will receive power from the 220 kV Ambetha Grid Substation of Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation Limited (GETCO). The entire electrical network will be monitored through a centralised control centre to ensure safe and reliable operations. The Surat–Bilimora section comprises approximately 50 km of elevated alignment between the two stations. The alignment includes bridges across four rivers and a steel bridge over National Highway 53 (NH-53). The viaduct is also equipped with approximately 94,000 noise barriers to minimise noise impact on the surrounding areas. Following the activation of the overhead electrical system, NHSRCL has issued a public safety advisory warning residents, commuters, construction workers and others against approaching or touching electrical installations or undertaking unauthorised work near the alignment. articles.title: Anantnag becomes India's first district to complete 1.57 lakh Digital Holistic Progress Cards
articles.content: Top Stories Anantnag becomes India’s first district to complete 1.57 lakh Digital Holistic Progress Cards Achieves 100% coverage across 1,444 govt, private schools; sets benchmark for competency-based learning, holistic assessment Arif Rashid 22 Nov 2026 03:52 IST Follow Us Srinagar, Nov 21: In a major milestone for the education sector, Anantnag district of Kashmir Division has become the first district in the country to complete 157,860 Digital Holistic Progress Cards (HPCs), covering 1,444 government and private schools, including CBSE-affiliated institutions. The achievement marks a significant step towards transforming the assessment system from conventional examination-based evaluation to a more comprehensive, competency-based approach that focuses on the overall development of students. An official of the School Education Department said the initiative was launched in May 2025, when the district began providing on-site academic support to teachers at cluster and school levels through faculty members of the District Institute of Education and Training (DIET) Anantnag. The programme focused on Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN), PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan, competency-based learning and the implementation of Holistic Progress Cards. "For nearly two years, our DIET resource teams conducted walkthroughs of the demo Holistic Progress Card available on the PARAKH portal. Thousands of teachers became familiar with its philosophy and framework during 2025 and 2026, even before the Ministry of Education introduced its digital version in August-September 2026," the official said. Recognising HPC as a transformative initiative in competency-based learning and assessment, the PARAKH Team Anantnag, under the leadership of the Chief Education Officer, Principal DIET and District Education Planning Officer (DEPO), devised a phased implementation strategy. The process began with PM SHRI Schools, followed by all government schools and subsequently private educational institutions. Initially, Heads of Institutions, teachers of PM SHRI Schools, School Nodal Officers (SNOs) and teachers from government and private institutions were oriented through online sessions about the philosophy of holistic assessment and its digital framework. However, realising that HPC implementation was much more than a routine data-entry exercise and required a fundamental understanding of pedagogical transformation, the district subsequently organised face-to-face training sessions, supported by continuous online and offline guidance. Zonal Master Trainers played a crucial role by extending on-call and on-site academic and technical assistance to teachers to ensure that the actual objectives of the initiative were understood and implemented effectively. "From school logins, teacher and student registrations, Parts A, B and C, summative marks, NCrF credit scores, APAAR logins, DigiLocker and the Academic Bank of Credits portal to the final generation and completion of HPCs, the journey has been extraordinary," the official said. He added that achieving 100 per cent completion in government schools in October and subsequently bringing every private school on board was a remarkable accomplishment. The official acknowledged that the actual spirit of the Holistic Progress Card lies in continuous assessment throughout the academic session rather than completing the exercise within a limited timeframe.
